bham-01-tip.caption:
Friday, half four, shutters coming down. Somebody is sat in the back with a folder and a mug of tea, writing down what the week took.

That is the habit. Invoices out while the job is still fresh in everyone's mind, receipts in one place instead of four, the takings written down on the day they happened. Twenty minutes, and nobody will ever congratulate you for it.

What it buys you is the ability to answer a question. What did last month actually make. Can the second van wait until spring. Is the quiet patch real, or does it only feel real because December is dark. An owner who can answer those makes decisions. An owner who cannot makes guesses.

Boring paperwork is not the opposite of ambition. It is what ambition stands on.

If yours is currently exciting, we can make it dull for you.
bham-01-tip.ask: Send this to the person who keeps saying they will sort it after Christmas.
bham-01-tip.title: Twenty minutes on a Friday with a folder and a mug of tea

bham-02-acq.caption:
Some things are easier in a room. You can post the bag of receipts, or you can bring it in, put it on the desk, and have somebody go through it with you while you drink a cup of tea.

We are at 22-42 Washwood Heath Road, Saltley, B8 1RB. A real door, on a road you already drive down. You can park, walk in, and ask the question you have been meaning to ask since April.

The first conversation is free and lasts 30 minutes. Bring whatever you have, in whatever state it is in. Nobody here is going to be shocked by a shoebox.
bham-02-acq.ask: Save this one so the address is in your phone when you need it.
bham-02-acq.title: A real door in Saltley you can bring your paperwork through

bham-03-acq.caption:
You should not have to teach your accountant your own job. If the first meeting goes on explaining what the Construction Industry Scheme is, why a contractor takes tax off your payment before it ever reaches you, why the van matters and why half the takings come in cash, you are paying somebody to learn.

We work with Birmingham trades every week: builders, electricians, plasterers, couriers, barbers, and the people who run the takeaways. We know what the records look like when a subcontractor starts on a Monday and is gone by the Friday, and we know what HMRC expects to see about it.

One fixed monthly fee, agreed before we start. We handle the handover from your old accountant and write the professional clearance letter ourselves, so you are not chasing anybody.

Come and talk to us for 30 minutes, free, and see how far we get.
bham-03-acq.ask: Share this with someone who is still doing their own books at midnight.
bham-03-acq.title: We already know how the deductions, the van and the cash takings work

bham-04-acq.caption:
Here is what being with us does to your January: nothing.

Your year-end accounts and your tax return are inside the monthly fee. There is no separate invoice when the year closes, because the work has been done through the year, a bit at a time, while the paperwork was still fresh and somebody could still remember the job.

We keep an eye on the dates as well. You will hear from us before something is due, not after. That is one of the quieter benefits of having somebody who answers the phone.

Thirty minutes, free, whenever suits you. Bring the last set of accounts if you can find them.
bham-04-acq.ask: Worth saving if you are not certain what your current fee actually covers.
bham-04-acq.title: Year-end is already inside the monthly fee

bham-05-edu.caption:
If you have people on the payroll, there is up to £10,500 you can take off the National Insurance you pay as their employer in 2026/27. It comes off your employer bill, not off anybody's wages.

And nobody sends it to you. You claim it yourself, through your payroll software, by sending what is called an Employment Payment Summary. The claim also does not roll forward: it has to be made again every tax year, so an employer who claimed last April and assumed it carried on has quietly lost a year of it. The old £100,000 eligibility cap was removed in April 2025.

The employers it does not cover:

— a limited company where the director is the only employee paid above the Secondary Threshold, the point at which employers' National Insurance starts
— a public authority that is not a charity
— an employer with half or more of its work in or for the public sector
— an employer of a nanny, cleaner or gardener, unless that person is a care or support worker
— every company but one in a group of connected companies
— an employer paying a worker under the off-payroll working rules, for those payments

If you run a shop, a garage or a takeaway with three or four on the payroll, it is five minutes of somebody's time to check.
bham-05-edu.ask: Save this for April, when the claim has to be made all over again.
bham-05-edu.title: Up to £10,500 off the National Insurance you pay on your staff

bham-06-edu.caption:
If you are the only adult living in your home, a quarter of your Council Tax bill can come off. That is the single person discount, 25%, and it applies in England and Wales.

It also applies when other adults do live with you and every one of them is, in the council's word, disregarded — someone the rules do not count when they add up the adults in a home. GOV.UK's list includes under-18s, some apprentices, 18 and 19 year olds in full-time education, full-time students, student nurses, live-in carers, people who are severely mentally impaired, and diplomats.

Other reductions sit alongside it. The Disabled Band Reduction Scheme charges the bill at one band lower, or takes 17% off a Band A home where there is no lower band, and it applies only where the home is larger than it would need to be if nobody disabled lived there. Where someone in the home is severely mentally impaired, which is GOV.UK's own term, a discount of 100%, 50% or 25% may apply, depending on who else lives there.

It stops at a second adult. Where two or more adults who are counted live in the property there is no single person discount, and income makes no difference either way: a household with two counted adults does not get it however little it earns. Second homes and long-term empty homes carry a premium instead. Scotland works to its own rules.

Nothing happens automatically. You apply to your own billing authority — Birmingham City Council, or Solihull, Sandwell, Dudley, Walsall, Wolverhampton or Coventry — and you tell them when somebody moves in, because the discount ends from that date.
bham-06-edu.ask: Save this and check your own bill before the next one lands.
bham-06-edu.title: 25% off Council Tax if you are the only adult in the house

bham-07-edu.caption:
Black Friday is on Friday. If you run a shop or a takeaway, you are about to put through hundreds of small sales, some with VAT on them and some without, and your till is not going to hand you the VAT on each one.

Where that is genuinely your situation, you are allowed to work the VAT out from a whole day's takings instead. The rules for doing it are the retail schemes, and there are five published ones: point of sale, two apportionment schemes and two direct calculation schemes. Point of sale means the till does the work, rate by rate. The other four work backwards from your takings and from what you bought or sold at each rate.

Three things to know. They are not a saving and they are not the Flat Rate Scheme; they are a way of totalling tax you already owe. For a published scheme there is no application and no permission — you simply use one you are eligible for. And they are only for retailers who cannot account for VAT the normal way, sale by sale: if your till already records the VAT on every sale, HMRC can refuse you a scheme, and can refuse one that does not give a fair and reasonable result.

The size limits. Apportionment scheme 1 and direct calculation scheme 1 are for retail sales, before VAT, of no more than £1 million. The other apportionment and direct calculation schemes run to £130 million. Above £130 million no published scheme is open to you and you agree a tailored one with HMRC.

Some sales never go through a scheme at all. Wholesale and trade sales need normal accounting. Apportionment scheme 1 cannot cover services or goods you made or grew yourself, apportionment scheme 2 cannot cover services or catering, and catering normally goes through point of sale.

Whichever you use, you keep a record of your daily gross takings, and under Making Tax Digital you keep it digitally.
bham-07-edu.ask: Save this before the weekend, while the till is still quiet.
bham-07-edu.title: Hundreds of small sales, mixed VAT rates, and five legal ways to total it

bham-08-joke.caption:
Sixty per cent off, a 65-inch television in the boot, and by the time it is through the front door it has become a business expense for client presentations.

The test is not the price and it is not how good the deal was. It is whether the business needed the thing and whether the business uses it. Something that lives in a front room and is watched by the family is not a business cost, whatever the receipt says.

The one that genuinely catches people is the mixed purchase: a laptop used for work and for everything else, a phone, a van that also does the weekend shop. Those are not all or nothing. There is a proportion that belongs to the business, and if you write down an honest estimate at the time, nobody has to argue about it a year later.

Buy the television if you want it. Buy it as yourself, and keep it out of the accounts.
bham-08-joke.ask: Share this with the person who already has their Black Friday list written.
bham-08-joke.title: The Black Friday television that somehow became a business expense

bham-09-joke.caption:
The van says ACE PLUMBING. The invoice says Ace Plumbing & Heating Services. The bank account says a company name somebody registered in 2014 and nobody has said out loud since.

Then a customer goes to pay, their banking app asks them to confirm the name on the account, and it does not match the invoice. So they ring you. You are under a sink. The money waits until Thursday.

It is the least glamorous reason invoices sit unpaid, and it costs nothing to fix. Decide what the business is called. Put that name on the invoice, and put the legal name underneath it where the two differ: your own name if you are a sole trader, or the registered company name and number if you are a limited company. Then make sure the bank account carries a name that matches, because the bank's check is on the account name and nothing else.

One name, three places, one afternoon. It gets you paid faster than any amount of chasing.
bham-09-joke.ask: Share this with the trade whose van, invoices and bank account all disagree.
bham-09-joke.title: Three names, one business, and a customer who cannot pay you

bham-10-quote.caption:
Epictetus was a slave in Rome before he was a philosopher, and he had no patience for the idea that anything worth having arrives finished.

The fig does not negotiate. It takes the time it takes. Blossom, then fruit, then ripening, and skipping a stage is not available.

A business is the same. The client list, the reputation on a street, the accounts that finally make sense — none of it appears in a week. It is built by somebody doing ordinary things repeatedly, in order, for longer than they wanted to.

If you are in the middle of that and it feels slow, it is not a sign you are doing it wrong.
bham-10-quote.ask: Share this with someone who is building something slowly.
bham-10-quote.title: Epictetus on why nothing good is built in a hurry
